key_insight: Hurricane-induced turbulence and mean wind structures vary strongly with LES grid resolution, and those differences materially change the aeroelastic loads on an idling wind turbine.
engineering_relevance: Accurate extreme-load prediction for turbines in tropical cyclone regions requires high-resolution inflow modeling, not just coarse storm-scale wind fields.
method: Performed large-eddy simulations of Hurricane Laura at three resolutions: 55.55 m, 25 m, and 10 m grid spacing.
Used LES output directly as inflow for aeroelastic wind turbine simulations.
Compared mean flow and turbulence structure across resolutions to assess resulting turbine response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports clear resolution-dependent differences in mean wind and turbulent structures, which produced distinct aeroelastic behavior in the turbine response.
watch_item: Results depend on simulated inflow fidelity, so lower-resolution LES may underpredict or mischaracterize extreme loading conditions.
paper_title: Hurricane Laura-induced loads on wind turbines -- Part I: High-fidelity modeling and sensitivity to turbulent inflow conditions
